---

If there were a Hall of Fame for hosting feasts, my mother’s name would be emblazoned near the top.

\[Sister K would not be far behind — though she still has a few years, or perhaps decades, to catch up.\]

Mom had several advantages.\

After a long day of worship, people arrived hungry, and any meal would have tasted good.\

An invitation that promised food was always appreciated — and seldom declined.

But as I would later learn, it wasn’t simply hunger or hospitality that drew such praise.\

It was my mother’s mastery — her deep knowledge of northern Korean cuisine, especially from the Pyongyang (평양, 平壤) tradition — that made each gathering memorable.

She made several dishes, a people's choice, that is hard to replicate.

오이김치, 홍어회 김치찌게

These dishes didn't rely on the heavy use of sauces, but instead used the natural flavor of each ingredients and made them reinforce and ultimately be part of the overall line-up of the feast.

She made several dishes that quickly became people’s favorites — the kind that are nearly impossible to replicate.

오이김치 (cucumber kimchi) and 홍어회 김치찌개 (fermented skate kimchi stew) were among her signature creations.

Her cooking never depended on heavy sauces or overpowering seasonings. Instead, she drew out the natural essence of each ingredient, letting their individual flavors harmonize — each one reinforcing the other until they came together in a single, memorable symphony of taste.

After the meal, conversation would flow freely.\

Because everyone was satisfied and at ease, words became lighter, kinder, and more meaningful.

It reminds me of the biblical accounts — of Jesus feeding the multitudes, and of Mary and Martha, one choosing the better part.\

Yet in this life, the physical and the spiritual are not separate.\

We must often be nourished in body before our spirits can truly listen.

My mother understood this intuitively and implemented rigorously.\

She chose both — preparing meals that opened hearts, and in doing so, prepared her guests to receive something higher.
